subject: DPA clarifications and next steps (PII, retention, breach notice)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Cooper <jane.cooper@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA clarifications and next steps (PII, retention, breach notice)

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and the items we agreed to follow up on: 

1) Controller / Processor roles: you asked us to confirm how Redwood classifies the parties for Acme Payments' integration (we expect we act as processor for customer-provided data; more detail below).
2) Subprocessors: you wanted a list of subprocessors and the notification cadence for changes.
3) Breach notice / incident response: timeline for notifications and contact points.
4) Data retention / deletion: options for retention windows and the mechanism to purge cached KV/prefix caches.
5) Data residency: requirement to pin logs/keys to US regions where applicable.

I've attached our current DPA (Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf) and a short security-summary.pdf that highlights logging and retention controls. Answers below are high-level — legal/security would want to sign off on any contract text, but this should help you prep.

Controller / Processor: Redwood operates as a processor for customer-provided content (PII, messages, etc.) under our hosted and dedicated offerings. We process on behalf of Acme and do not assert ownership over customer content. For Private deployments where the customer runs the runtime in their VPC/on-prem, Redwood is typically a service provider / vendor.

Subprocessors: We maintain a list of subprocessors in Appendix A of the DPA; we notify customers 30 days prior to material additions and provide an opt-out right for the newly added subprocessor for enterprise customers on a case-by-case basis.

Breach notice: Redwood commits to notifying customers within 72 hours of identifying a security incident that materially affects customer data, with updates as we investigate. Our incident response slides in the security-summary.pdf include escalation contacts.

Retention / deletion: You can configure retention windows per-route. For hosted customers we retain request logs and traces for 90 days by default; embeddings and model outputs can be disabled/purged on request. We support API calls and a managed deletion workflow for prefix/KV cache eviction.

Next steps: 1) Please confirm which items you want reflected in contract language. 2) If Acme Legal has redlines, you can route to legal@redwood.com and I'll loop in Rishi (our GC) and Dev for technical closure. 3) If helpful, we can run a short session with your security team next week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf (15 pages)
Attachment: security-summary.pdf (4 pages)

Subject: Re: DPA clarifications and next steps (PII, retention, breach notice)

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick recap and attachments. A few clarifying Qs from Acme Legal / Security: 

- For controller/processor: can you confirm the exact language you recommend for the DPA where Redwood is listed as "Processor"? Our legal team prefers explicit wording around processing instructions and not engaging subprocessors without notice.
- Subprocessors: can you share the current list? We need to see any cloud infra providers and analytics vendors. Also want to know the cadence and whether a 30-day notice is contractual or policy.
- Breach notice: 72 hours is OK as a starting point — does Redwood commit to providing root cause and remediation plan within 30 days?
- Retention: we need a 30-day default for request logs (rather than 90) for production environment that touches PII. Is that configurable or would that be a custom enterprise setting?

Also — can you send the DPA with tracked changes or point us to a DocuSign link if you prefer we sign and then propose redlines?

Jane
Head of Procurement, Acme Payments

Jane —

Answers inline below. I'm copying Rishi (GC) for legal wording and Dev for the retention/tech details.

- Recommended DPA language: We can include a short clause that states: "Customer is the Controller and Redwood Inference, Inc. is a Processor acting on Customer's documented instructions; Redwood will not process Customer Data for any purpose other than to provide the Services set forth in the agreement." Rishi, please review and suggest legal-approved phrasing if we need something more prescriptive.

- Subprocessor list: current subprocessors are listed in Appendix A of the attached DPA; key entries include AWS (us-west-2), GCP (us-central1) for optional dedicated deployments, Datadog (monitoring), and SendGrid (email notifications). Dev — can you confirm the infra zones and whether we can commit to US-only infra for Acme?

- Notice cadence: the 30-day notice is a policy; we can include it contractually for enterprise deals.

- Breach follow-up timing: Redwood will provide an initial notification within 72 hours and aim to provide a root cause and remediation plan within 30 days. We'll add language that updates will be provided as available. Rishi — confirm if 30-day remediation commitment is acceptable.

- Retention: For hosted production we default to 90 days, but enterprise customers can request a 30-day retention window as a configurable setting. Dev — please add technical notes for how we enforce that and any cost/feature tradeoffs (e.g., reduced tracing history).

Next steps: 
1) Jane / Acme Legal: if you want tracked DPA redlines, reply with your preferred method (DocuSign link or email redlines).
2) Rishi & Dev: I'll switch to a legal thread if Acme wants to propose specific text.

Thanks,
Marissa
